extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is the first training environment for software engineering agents, containing 2,438 real-world task instances sourced from 11 popular open-source Python repositories. Each instance comprises a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a natural language task description derived from GitHub issues.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Repositories were filtered using SEART GitHub search based on criteria (created before July 1, 2022, >500 stars, ≥300 lines of code, >500 PRs, >100 contributors). Task instances were extracted from pull requests using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script. Executable environments were manually configured, and instances were validated using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script. The process required approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Instances that failed execution-based validation were filtered out, resulting in 2,438 validated instances from an initial pool.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Pull requests from 11 popular Python GitHub repositories, including associated issues, code diffs (git patches), unit tests, and repository configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt, pyproject.toml).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Semi-manual creation of executable environments, manual configuration of dependencies for each task instance using configuration files, CI scripts, or repository documentation. Validation performed using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than original code.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Execution-based validation ensuring gold patches pass more unit tests than original code; instances failing validation were filtered out, resulting in 2,438 unit-test-validated instances.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEART GitHub Search for repository filtering; SWE-Bench's instance extraction script for converting repositories into task instances; SWE-Bench's versioning script for version association; SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script for instance verification.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern, with pandas comprising nearly one-third of total tasks and bokeh representing only one percent. The dataset includes sophisticated repositories like pandas and MONAI which may contribute to decreased model performance compared to SWE-Bench.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited to Python repositories and 11 specific open-source projects. Tasks in SWE-Gym are on average harder than SWE-Bench. Models show consistently lower performance on SWE-Gym compared to SWE-Bench, possibly due to overfitting to SWE-Bench or inclusion of sophisticated repositories. Training performance is currently limited by compute budget for sampling rather than the number of tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: SWE-Gym enables training of software engineering agents that can automatically resolve GitHub issues, potentially automating software development tasks and accelerating research in learning-based software engineering agents.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: SWE-Gym is designed for training and evaluating software engineering agents and verifier models. Use cases include: (1) training LM-based SWE agents via rejection sampling fine-tuning, (2) training outcome-supervised reward models (verifiers) for inference-time scaling, (3) self-improvement of LMs through agent-environment interaction, and (4) rapid prototyping via SWE-Gym Lite. SWE-Gym Raw supports future research in SWE agent development and automatic dataset synthesis.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: SWE-Gym, models, and agent trajectories are publicly released. Pre-built Docker images for each instance are released, totaling 6 TB. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: SWE-Gym Lite subset of 230 instances was created by filtering out tasks requiring editing more than one file, tasks with poorly described problem statements, those with excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Repositories were filtered by creation date (before July 1, 2022), stars (>500), lines of code (≥300), pull requests (>500), and contributors (>100). Task instances were extracted using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script. Instances were versioned and associated with version numbers. Executable environments with pre-installed dependencies were manually configured using configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or repository documentation. Instances were validated using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than the original code, filtering out failed instances to yield 2,438 validated instances.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: SWE-Gym can be used to build strong learning-based agents, accelerating research in this area... Our work addresses this gap with SWE-Gym, a training environment based on real-world software engineering tasks that uses expert-written tests as reward signals. Our experiments demonstrate that SWE-Gym can build strong SWE agents without prompt engineering.
